summary: Module 3 VERIFY: Convention Matching. Ran the Convention Checklist against the agent's team code (team_router.py, teams_service.py, schemas/team.py from M2's Task 2) using the existing links.py / links_service.py / schemas/auth.py as the codebase ground truth. NAMING: router file team_router.py matches links.py/auth.py/analytics.py pattern; function names create_team/add_member/list_members/update_member_role/remove_member are verb-first like create_link/list_links/delete_link; _team_response/_member_response match the _to_response helper convention; schema class names CreateTeamRequest/TeamResponse/MemberResponse mirror CreateLinkRequest/LinkResponse. ERROR HANDLING: HTTPException raised in the service layer (links_service.py raises HTTPException 404 'link not found'; teams_service.py raises HTTPException 403/404/409 the same way), and main.py's exception handler wraps every HTTPException in error_envelope -- so error response format is identical by construction. Status codes 201/204/400/403/404/409 match the REST conventions used elsewhere (create 201, delete 204). IMPORTS/DEPENDENCIES: uses get_db + get_current_user + Depends exactly like links.py (no invented auth dependency); EmailStr is ALREADY used in schemas/auth.py and email-validator==2.3.0 is pinned in requirements.txt -- NO new dependency was added; agent reused the existing helper rather than inventing a duplicate validation function. FILE ORGANIZATION: router in app/routers/, service in app/services/, schema in app/schemas/ -- matches the controller+service+model split exactly; no monolithic file. MATCHES: 3+ conventions match perfectly in every category. MISMATCHES: zero in the final corrected code. Lesson: the M2 interface-contract correction made the context package complete -- the original Task 2 prompt (missing local context: actual schema) WOULD have produced a mismatch (owner_id column, invented resolution), which is exactly the failure mode the module predicts for an incomplete context package. The layering of architectural (error_envelope, router/service/schema split) + local (actual schema files) + constraint (roles, owner_id presentational) context produced output that looks like it belongs.
